annotations.title: Start a Chorus book, and get the one link to forward.

description: Starts a book of voice, video and written messages and returns its handle and the single link the organiser sends to everyone taking part. The book is for one person or a couple, or it goes by a title when it is for nobody in particular: a family’s recipes, a class’s year, a team’s goodbye. Gathering is free, and the people recording need no app and no account. Without organiser_email the book is made at once with nobody signing in, and the result carries keep_link, the page where the organiser reads the messages, has Chorus email people and orders the book. With organiser_email and no code, Chorus emails the organiser a six digit code; with organiser_email and the code, the book is made in their account.

answer_with.description: Any of voice, video and written. Voice and written when not said.

closes_on.description: Optional. The day collecting stops, as 2026-11-14. Without it the book stays open until it is closed, and a date can be set at any time after. A printed copy wanted for a day needs collecting to stop three weeks before it.

code.description: The six digit code emailed to the organiser. Without it, Chorus emails one.

expecting.description: Who is expected to record, by name or role, without email addresses. The book’s status names the ones still out.

lead_with.description: Which of those is the big button on a contributor’s phone.

occasion.description: A big birthday, A wedding, A new baby, As they grow, In memory, or Something else. Plain words are matched to one of those.

organiser_email.description: The organiser’s email address, for a book made in their Chorus account, which they open with a six digit code. Without it the book starts with no sign-in.

questions.description: The questions everybody answers, up to 12, each one line of up to 200 characters that a person can answer out loud in a minute or two. In a book with subject_name, {name} in a question becomes that name. When this is left out, a book with subject_name gets the set for the occasion and a book with only a title gets three open questions.

steps.description: What each person is given, in order, one screen each, when the book needs more than questions. Each step is { kind, text }: words (a question answered by voice, video or writing, text required), song (they search for it or paste a Spotify, YouTube or Apple Music link; it prints as the page's heading with a code that plays it), photo, voice (a voice note that prints as a code on their page), date, choice (with choices, two to eight), link (prints as a code), name (who it is from; first when left out). text is the screen's question, with {name} for the person; without it, a song, photo, voice or name screen carries Chorus's own wording. optional: false makes a photo, voice, date, choice or link one they cannot skip. Each person's answers make one page. Steps outrank questions. Example for a song book: [{kind:'song'},{kind:'words',text:'Why does it remind you of {name}?'},{kind:'photo'},{kind:'voice'},{kind:'name'}].

subject_name.description: Who the book is for, when it is for one person or a couple, as the organiser says it, for example Mum. A book needs subject_name, title or both, and a book for one person needs only subject_name.

title.description: The book’s title, in the person’s words, for example The Kelly family recipes. One line, up to 40 characters.
